channels.cardiac_respiratory: name='cardiac_respiratory' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=2 units='arbitrary' clock='physio_500hz' operator=None note='Pulse oximeter and respiration belt, 500 Hz, concurrent with BOLD for 3 of the 4 participants on disk (21 localizer physio files). A second KIND of boundary output -- autonomic rather than motor -- and the one the public copy means by "heart rate". Declared and NOT consumed: this whole card is disabled, so nothing here reaches a loss.'
channels.eyegaze: name='eyegaze' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=4 units='normalized_screen_coordinates' clock='physio_1000hz' operator=None note='x, y, pupil dilation, movie frame index at 1000 Hz. Present in the release for ses-movie ONLY, whose BOLD was not fetched, so it is concurrent with no imaging on disk. Declared because the release carries it; unusable here for a reason of fetch scope rather than licence.'

ds000113_real.notes: 7T whole-brain localizer fMRI (retinotopy x4 and a movie localizer) from the studyforrest project, 4 of 20 participants fetched. Blocked on a licence, not on data or on code: the parcellated cache exists and the coverage is measured. Resolving this means obtaining a licence statement that is in the bytes we hold -- a versioned snapshot that carries one, or a written statement from the authors -- not repeating the draft record's CC0 until it hardens into a fact.

channels.button_press: name='button_press' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=1 units='category' clock='elekta_meg_amp' operator=None note='Two-alternative in-scanner button press, recovered from STI101 response bits 256 and 4096. Measured 113 responses to 146 stimuli in one run, median RT 0.751 s, all within 0.2-2.0 s of their stimulus. A response whose latency falls outside 0.15-2.5 s is DROPPED rather than attributed to a different trial.'
channels.response_time: name='response_time' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=1 units='s' clock='elekta_meg_amp' operator=None note="Scored as log RT with the head's own predicted variance, as a separate term from the choice: collapsing them lets a confident-and-wrong RT be paid for by an easy choice."

ds000117_behaviour.notes: The two buttons are far from balanced -- 105 to 22 on the measured run -- so the majority-class rate is logged beside the choice accuracy. An accuracy read without it looks like learning when it is the prior. Licence CC0-1.0, stated in the snapshot's own dataset_description.json. n = 2 participants: this source exercises the boundary_output attachment and supports no population-level behavioural claim.

channels.eeg: name='eeg' attachment='observation' n_channels=70 units='V' clock='elekta_meg_amp' operator='lead_field' note='Digitised electrode positions, averaged over the 2 fetched participants; the mean electrode deviates 3.23 mm from that average, which bounds the individual head geometry this single operator discards.'
channels.face_stimulus: name='face_stimulus' attachment='stimulus' n_channels=1 units='category' clock='elekta_meg_amp' operator=None note='Famous / unfamiliar / scrambled face onsets, on STI101. A stimulus, NOT a boundary output and NOT an observation: it is known independently of the participant and carries no likelihood over latent state on its own. It is declared so the attachment report can say a stimulus stream exists; it is not currently consumed by a loss, and the report says that too.'

ds000117_real.notes: n = 2. Upstream ships 16 participants; this snapshot pinned 2 complete ones and the remaining 14 were not fetched. Two participants cannot estimate a between-participant variance, so no population-level claim may cite this source's n -- it contributes a second measured montage and a second recording site, which is what it is for.

ds002336_real.notes: The only fully paired episode in the register (body.tex 6.4): EEG at 5000 Hz and BOLD at 0.5 Hz on the same subject in the same 20 s block, a 10,000:1 rate ratio. Pairing is complete for 53 of 56 (subject, task) runs; the three unpaired runs are excluded from cross-modal terms, never half-imputed.

channels.eeg: name='eeg' attachment='observation' n_channels=64 units='V' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator='lead_field' note='Post-pulse scalp potential. Scored outside the artefact window only, by MASK -- the rollout still integrates through the excluded interval, so the operator is never asked to cross a discontinuity it did not produce.'
channels.tms_pulse: name='tms_pulse' attachment='stimulus' n_channels=1 units='percent_of_resting_motor_threshold' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator=None note='The intervention. A stimulus: known independently of the participant, and never evidence about latent state on its own. Onsets are exact on the amplifier sample clock (events.tsv carries an integer sample column). Intensity is DECLARED 100% rMT; the per-participant rMT in stimulator output units is not distributed, so no absolute dose exists and no intensity slope is estimable -- exactly one level is present.'
channels.emg: name='emg' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=2 units='V' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator=None note='The motor evoked potential. Used to RECOVER the stimulated hemisphere (paired per-trial log ratio of FDI peak-to-peak, right over left, in a 15-45 ms window). A run whose laterality falls below the stated effect-size floor is skipped, not labelled with the sign of a noisy mean. Not consumed by a likelihood.'

ds004024_perturb.notes: Two resolution bounds travel with every number read off this source. The model's fast clock is 8 ms, so TEP components earlier than N45 are below its temporal resolution and are not claimed; N100 and P180 are resolvable. And the first 10 ms after each pulse is masked out of the likelihood, blanked before filtering, because a zero-phase 0.5 Hz high-pass smears a 0.5 V step backwards across the whole epoch -- measured, and it rejected every epoch before it was fixed. At n = 2 with one target site and one intensity, this source supports "the model was trained on measured stimulation and predicts a measured evoked response" and nothing about generalising to an unseen perturbation.

channels.eeg: name='eeg' attachment='observation' n_channels=64 units='V' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator='lead_field' note="Recorded at 20 kHz in DC mode and brought to the model's 125 Hz here. Average-referenced, matching the founding montage."
channels.emg: name='emg' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=2 units='V' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator=None note='First dorsal interosseous EMG, left and right. A boundary output: muscle activity the participant produced, measured outside the skull. DECLARED AND NOT CONSUMED by a loss in run 3 -- it is used upstream, by derive_stimulated_hemisphere, to recover which M1 was stimulated. That is a use, not a likelihood, and the attachment report distinguishes them.'
channels.ecg: name='ecg' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=1 units='V' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator=None note='Autonomic. Declared, present on disk, not consumed by a loss in run 3.'
channels.eog: name='eog' attachment='boundary_output' n_channels=2 units='V' clock='ds004024.brainvision_amp' operator=None note='Ocular. Declared, present on disk, not consumed by a loss in run 3.'

ds004024_rest_real.notes: n = 2. Upstream ships binaries for all 13 participants; this snapshot pinned a 2-participant subset, and the absence is our fetch choice rather than an upstream gap. These are the same two participants the perturbation card uses, which is what lets a stimulated response be compared against that participant's own unstimulated baseline.

eegmmidb_real.notes: Scalp EEG during rest, real and imagined movement. Single site, single montage, no individual head models: supports population-level EEG prediction claims only. 290,673 windows on disk; the leakage-audited split is 189,765/29,238/71,670 windows over 71/11/27 of the 109 participants (train_main.log lines 22, 126-129).

montage_calibration.notes: Per-channel gain/offset/noise nuisance for the EEG head. Its mask is contained in eegmmidb_real's, which is what makes it admissible at tier 2 rather than a second founding source.

negative_control_shuffled.notes: Amplitude-matched, phase-randomised surrogates of the real EEG windows.

sim_wholebrain.notes: Delayed connectome-coupled neural-mass SDEs (Wilson-Cowan, Jansen-Rit, reduced Wong-Wang, Stuart-Landau, linear Gaussian). 37 shards, 37,888 trajectories, 454,656 trajectory-seconds, 49 GB, fast tier only. Generated on the SYNTHETIC ellipsoid connectome (index_fast.json anatomy.provenance = synthetic_fallback, 454 regions), not on the 414-parcel ENIGMA/HCP prior: the shapes differ, so adopting the real prior requires regenerating the corpus. 40.69 % of it carries no anatomy-derived regional timescale (as generated).

channels.eeg_bipolar: name='eeg_bipolar' attachment='observation' n_channels=2 units='V' clock='sleep_edf_psg' operator='bipolar_lead_field' note='Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz. BIPOLAR derivations, not monopolar potentials, and never average-referenced: the mean of two bipolar derivations is not a reference and subtracting it would mix frontal and occipital signals into each other.'

sleepedf_real.notes: 7.60 GB and 78 participants on disk, whole-night home polysomnograms at 100 Hz. Open Data Commons Attribution Licence (ODC-By 1.0); cite Kemp et al. 2000 and Goldberger et al. 2000. This is the ONLY corpus here with a genuine future-session holdout -- night 1 to night 2 -- and therefore the only source that could ever support a G5 individualisation claim. Run 3 does not make one: it inherits run 2's participant-disjoint split, on which no held-out person has a fitted person effect, so individualisation is unmeasurable by construction.
